newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 24.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- John Walter is taking swift, bold actions at AT&T just six weeks after joining the company - rushing to centralize control over the company's six business units.
- Mercantile Bancorp agreed to buy Roosevelt Financial Group for $1.07 billion.
- Nationwide filed with the SEC to raise $500 million by selling up to a 20 percent stake in its life insurance unit through an IPO.
- The treasury will postpone the initial offering of its "iniflation-indexed" bonds because of complications in setting the terms for the new product.
- West coast ports are suffering from cargo-handling problems that shippers blame on longshoremen's "go-slow" tactics.
- Consumers' incomes rebounded last month from a weak October.
The IRS proposed rule changes to ease mergers and acquisitions through tax-free exchanges of shares.
- Though auditors are required under a new law to aggressively seek to detect "illegal acts" affecting a company's financial statements.
- Ira sorkin plans to resign as chief legal officer for Nomura's U.S. unit.
- Corporate boards can help insulate themselves from some shareholder suits by creating compliance systems to detect corporate wrongdoing.
- Archer Daniels reached a definitive agreement to buy W.R. Grace 's cocoa business for $430 million.
